selectedFragments.text:
Recovery traffic after an outage

When many clients wake together, doubling every waiting interval still leaves them in step. Our load rehearsal had quiet gaps followed by sharp bursts. Give each caller an independently sampled pause between zero and its current ceiling. Increase that ceiling after a failure, with a cap and an overall deadline. The random generator should not receive the same seed in every container. Record attempt counts and elapsed time, not just the final status. A server hint may impose a minimum wait. This is traffic shaping during recovery; it does not make a side effect safe to execute twice.

headingPath: Loss on one stream should not stall another
match.preview: Loss on one stream should not stall another HTTP/2 multiplexes requests over a TCP connection, but a missing TCP segment holds later bytes until recovery. Independent application streams can therefore wait behind a loss affecting that conne

selectedFragments.text:
Loss on one stream should not stall another

HTTP/2 multiplexes requests over a TCP connection, but a missing TCP segment holds later bytes until recovery. Independent application streams can therefore wait behind a loss affecting that connection. QUIC transports streams with independent ordered delivery, so missing data on one stream need not block delivery on unrelated streams.

This does not eliminate congestion control or delays in the affected stream. Shared network capacity still constrains all traffic. Compare traces under packet loss rather than treating the protocol name as a speed guarantee. Application dependencies can also force one request to wait for another.

selectedFragments.text:
Admission control at the gateway

A token bucket allows short bursts while enforcing an average request rate. Incoming work spends a token; when the bucket is empty the gateway rejects or queues it within a bounded waiting period. Keep queue length, token refill rate and concurrent workers as separate controls.

Per-account quotas stop one tenant from consuming the entire service. They do not coordinate client timers after an outage. Capacity planning uses arrival rate and service time, while retry policy belongs to the caller. Dashboards should distinguish initial attempts from repeated traffic.

A scheduler grants workers leases so abandoned jobs can eventually be claimed by another process. Heartbeats extend a lease while work progresses. Dashboards show the holder and expiration time. A stalled process can resume after a long pause, and its local belief about ownership may be old. Clock displays help investigation but do not by themselves establish authority to publish an output. Operators should keep the original job identifiers while examining such an incident.

selectedFragments.text:
The response vanished after submission

Before sending an external job, persist its stable operation identifier and a reserved state. If the connection closes after transmission, mark the outcome unknown. Ask the provider for the receipt using that identifier before considering another submission. A missing client response is not proof that the provider did no work or charged nothing.

Keep confirmed, failed-before-send and uncertain states distinct. A local process restart reloads the ledger and blocks uncertain operations. Where the provider has no lookup or idempotency guarantee, manual reconciliation may be necessary. A new identifier would hide the uncertainty rather than resolve it.

Remote transcription queue

A simple retry timer

The small downloader waits one, two, four and eight seconds after consecutive connection failures. Deterministic intervals make its tests easy to reproduce. After four attempts it stops and shows the last transport status. A successful request resets the counter.

This schedule works for a single unattended client, but a fleet started at the same time can retry together. Raising the maximum delay reduces average load without necessarily removing those peaks. The download is read-only, and temporary files are renamed only after the checksum passes. Other operations need their own repeat-safety policy.

Electing a scheduler

Only one active scheduler should assign ordinary work at a time. A lease with periodic heartbeats can make a replacement possible after the original machine disappears. The lease duration trades faster recovery against more false suspicion during pauses.

An expired lease changes who may claim new work, but does not physically stop an old process that later wakes. This note describes election and monitoring, not a storage-side mechanism for rejecting its writes. Keep leadership changes visible and avoid using wall-clock log order as proof of which process acted first.

selectedFragments.text:
Retryable and permanent failures

A read request may be repeated after a temporary connection failure within a fixed deadline. Authentication failures and invalid input generally require a change before another attempt. A response telling the client to slow down should influence scheduling.

Classifying a transport failure as temporary does not establish whether a remote write happened. The operation's repeat-safety contract must be checked separately. Collect attempt count and final status without logging credentials or full user payloads. Retry policy should remain bounded even during a long outage.

Holding a row while making a decision

SELECT FOR UPDATE obtains a row lock until the transaction ends. Other conflicting writers wait or fail according to their timeout. This is useful for a short critical section that must inspect and change shared state together.

Do not hold the transaction open while a person studies a form. Long-held locks increase contention and can participate in deadlocks. A lock timeout is not evidence that an update succeeded. Systems with long think time often need a different concurrency strategy.

Expanding review intervals

Repeated retrieval should be separated in time. After an unaided correct response, lengthen the next interval; after an error, bring the item back sooner and inspect the prompt. Schedule by observed recall rather than the date on which a card was created.

One fixed calendar for every word ignores differences in difficulty. A missed review is not a reason to restart the entire deck. Limit the daily workload and suspend ambiguous cards until they are rewritten. The scheduler determines when practice occurs; it cannot turn a recognition-only exercise into productive recall.

headingPath: Rejecting stale edits without a held lock
match.preview: Rejecting stale edits without a held lock Read a record together with its revision. Submit the update with that expected revision, and make the database replace it only if the revision still matches. Increment the revision on success; zero

selectedFragments.text:
Rejecting stale edits without a held lock

Read a record together with its revision. Submit the update with that expected revision, and make the database replace it only if the revision still matches. Increment the revision on success; zero affected rows means someone else changed the record and the editor must reload or merge.

This compare-and-swap pattern prevents a lost update without keeping a lock throughout a person's editing session. A timestamp with poor precision is a weak substitute for a revision counter. The conflict belongs in the user workflow; blindly retrying the old replacement would erase the protection.

selectedFragments.text:
One purchase, one operation identity

Assign an idempotency key to a business operation before its first POST. Store the key with a hash of the parameters and the eventual result on the server. A retry with the same key and same parameters returns that recorded result instead of creating a second purchase. Reusing the key for different parameters is rejected.

Deduplicating identical files or comparing request bodies is insufficient: two intentional purchases can have identical details. The identity must survive a client restart. If the first response is lost, query that identity or retry only under the server's documented idempotency contract.

selectedFragments.text:
Несколько потоков поверх QUIC

QUIC использует UDP как транспорт для защищённого соединения и предоставляет приложению отдельные потоки. Потеря данных одного потока не требует останавливать доставку уже доступных данных другого. Это отличается от общего упорядоченного потока байтов TCP.

Потери всё равно требуют восстановления, а управление перегрузкой остаётся общим ограничением. Переход на новый протокол не исправит медленную обработку на сервере. При измерениях разделяйте установление соединения, передачу и время приложения.

selectedFragments.text:
SQLite readers during normal writes

Write-ahead logging lets a read transaction see a stable snapshot while another connection appends changes. Enable WAL mode deliberately, keep read transactions short, and let checkpointing reclaim the log when readers release their snapshots. This provides live queries without copying database files or holding a long exclusive lock against writers.

There is still only one writer at a time. Long readers can prevent checkpoint progress and make the WAL file grow. Treat the database, WAL and shared-memory files as a coordinated system; copying one live file is not a backup procedure. Measure transaction duration before tuning timeouts.

Resolvers cache negative answers as well as successful lookups. After an NXDOMAIN response, a newly created DNS record may remain invisible to that resolver until the negative cache lifetime expires. match.preview: Reconstructing state from an event log An append-only sequence of accepted events can rebuild a projection after a crash. Save a projection checkpoint only after its state is durable, then replay events after that position. Event identity a

selectedFragments.text:
Reconstructing state from an event log

An append-only sequence of accepted events can rebuild a projection after a crash. Save a projection checkpoint only after its state is durable, then replay events after that position. Event identity and ordering rules matter when delivery is repeated.

Replaying a projection is different from resubmitting an external action. The event records what was accepted, while a vanished remote response may leave that fact unknown. Keep side effects out of an unguarded replay loop. Snapshots speed recovery but should be verifiable against their log position.

Numbered pages in a small report

LIMIT with OFFSET is convenient for a small, stable result set and for jumping to a numbered page. The database skips the offset rows before returning the requested portion. Large offsets can become expensive.

If new entries appear ahead of the current page, rows can repeat or be skipped between requests. A unique order avoids ambiguous ties but does not prevent the positions from shifting. For an immutable report generated from a fixed snapshot, numbered pages can still be a reasonable interface.

headingPath: Durable progress in a batch converter
match.preview: Durable progress in a batch converter Our image converter processes a directory overnight. It writes each completed output to a temporary file, verifies it, then renames it and records the input checksum and completed position in a durable

selectedFragments.text:
Durable progress in a batch converter

Our image converter processes a directory overnight. It writes each completed output to a temporary file, verifies it, then renames it and records the input checksum and completed position in a durable checkpoint. On restart it verifies recorded outputs and continues from the last committed boundary rather than beginning the directory again.

The checkpoint and output must agree. A counter advanced before a file is durable could skip work after a power loss. This design handles local, repeatable transformations. An external paid action whose response disappeared needs a receipt lookup; a local checkpoint alone cannot establish whether that action happened.

match.preview: Reclaiming space in SQLite Deleting rows usually leaves pages available for reuse inside the database file. VACUUM rebuilds the database to compact it, requiring temporary disk space and coordination with other activity. It is a maintenance

selectedFragments.text:
Reclaiming space in SQLite

Deleting rows usually leaves pages available for reuse inside the database file. VACUUM rebuilds the database to compact it, requiring temporary disk space and coordination with other activity. It is a maintenance operation, not a way to make continuous readers coexist with writes.

Schedule compaction after checking file growth and operational needs. Automatic vacuum settings have different overhead and must be chosen deliberately. Keeping a small file on disk is not always worth a disruptive rebuild. Backups and integrity checks serve separate purposes.

match.preview: Keeping a backup out of the failure domain A disk permanently attached to the same writable system can be damaged by the same mistake or malicious process as the source. Rotate an offline local copy and retain several dated generations. Dis

selectedFragments.text:
Keeping a backup out of the failure domain

A disk permanently attached to the same writable system can be damaged by the same mistake or malicious process as the source. Rotate an offline local copy and retain several dated generations. Disconnect it after verification so ordinary deletions cannot immediately propagate to every copy.

This improves isolation but is not proof that the files can be restored or decrypted. A separate recovery rehearsal checks that. Decide how much recent work may be lost between rotations, label the generations, and inspect disk health without treating health statistics as a substitute for reading the data.

selectedFragments.text:
Restarting a disposable build

The documentation preview is built in a temporary directory. If compilation fails, discard that directory and run the build from its clean inputs. No user edits live there, and outputs are cheap to regenerate. This avoids complicated partial-state recovery.

The strategy is unsuitable for an overnight conversion whose completed files are expensive to recreate. Keep the build input revision and compiler version in the log. A successful build replaces the published preview atomically, so visitors never see a half-written page.

selectedFragments.text:
Invalidating a cached view

A cache entry represents a particular input revision. After the underlying record changes, either remove the entry or write it under a new revision key. A short expiration time limits staleness but does not prove immediate consistency.

Watch for a slow old computation publishing after a newer update. Checking the expected revision when storing the result can reject that stale publication. This is related to concurrency control, although an in-process cache does not automatically enforce authority at an external storage service. Metrics should distinguish misses, evictions and rejected stale writes.

selectedFragments.text:
Shadowing a short recording

Invalidating a cached view

A cache entry represents a particular input revision. After the underlying record changes, either remove the entry or write it under a new revision key. A short expiration time limits staleness but does not prove immediate consistency.

headingPath: Keeping a backup out of the failure domain

selectedFragments.text:
Keeping a backup out of the failure domain

A disk permanently attached to the same writable system can be damaged by the same mistake or malicious process as the source. Rotate an offline local copy and retain several dated generations. Disconnect it after verification so ordinary deletions cannot immediately propagate to every copy.

This improves isolation but is not proof that the files can be restored or decrypted. A separate recovery rehearsal checks that. Local snapshots that survive a mistaken deletion

Keep dated backup generations on a separate local disk. A snapshot tool can hard-link unchanged files while preserving older directory trees; deleting a source file must not remove its prior generations. Retention removes old snapshots only according to an explicit schedule.

A synchronized mirror usually propagates deletions, so it cannot by itself recover yesterday's accidentally removed file. Electing a scheduler

Only one active scheduler should assign ordinary work at a time. A lease with periodic heartbeats can make a replacement possible after the original machine disappears. The lease duration trades faster recovery against more false suspicion during pauses.

An expired lease changes who may claim new work, but does not physically stop an old process that later wakes. This note describes election and monitoring, not a storage-side mechanism for rejecting its writes. Keep leadership changes visible and avoid using wall-clock log order as proof of which process acted first.

Reconstructing state from an event log

An append-only sequence of accepted events can rebuild a projection after a crash. Save a projection checkpoint only after its state is durable, then replay events after that position. Event identity and ordering rules matter when delivery is repeated.

Hosted OCR for a shared archive

The archive team uploads scanned pages to a cloud OCR service and receives searchable text with confidence scores. A central queue makes it convenient to process large batches from several computers. Language detection and layout analysis are performed by the remote provider.

headingPath: Durable progress in a batch converter
match.preview: Durable progress in a batch converter Our image converter processes a directory overnight. It writes each completed output to a temporary file, verifies it, then renames it and records the input checksum and completed position in a durable

selectedFragments.text:
Durable progress in a batch converter

Our image converter processes a directory overnight. Off-site version history

selectedFragments.text:
Can an encrypted backup be recovered?

Encryption protects backup contents only if the recovery secret remains available to the owner. Store a recovery copy of that secret separately from the machine and verify that the documented unlock procedure works on a clean test environment. A successful upload or copy does not prove decryptability.

Hard links and symbolic links

A hard link names the same underlying file data within a filesystem. A symbolic link stores a path that is resolved when followed. Moving a target can break a symbolic link, while editing data through one hard link affects the shared file.

Remote transcription queue

A cloud conversation service can reply to open-ended language exercises and suggest more natural wording. The client sends the learner's messages to the provider, even if the interface caches the conversation locally. An account and active connection are required for new replies.

Use invented examples when exploring the service. Corrections are suggestions to discuss, not authoritative grammar judgments. Downloading the chat history does not turn future inference into offline processing. A dictionary and a conversation partner solve different learning tasks.

selectedFragments.text:
A travel laptop can recognize photographed labels after the OCR binary and language files have been installed. The local command takes an image path and writes text to a sibling file. Disconnecting the network during a trial confirms that recognition itself has no server dependency.

This note is a compact field checklist, not an installation guide. Check that the expected language pack exists, retain the photo, and correct uncertain characters manually. Downloading missing components while travelling may be impossible. A translation service is a separate step and may send the resulting text elsewhere.

selectedFragments.text:
Transcribing a practice recording locally

A speech recognizer can process an audio file on the workstation when its model files are already available. Run a short synthetic recording first and inspect the transcript manually. The transcription process can then run with the network disconnected.

This workflow accepts audio, not scanned pages. It needs enough memory and compute for the selected model. Keep the original recording and avoid treating a plausible transcript as a verbatim record without review. Downloading model files is preparation, separate from sending recordings to a service.

match.preview: Remote transcription queue A hosted speech service accepts uploaded recordings and returns transcripts asynchronously. Store the provider's job identifier, check its status and retrieve the result when complete. Uploading twice after a lost

selectedFragments.text:
Remote transcription queue

A hosted speech service accepts uploaded recordings and returns transcripts asynchronously. Store the provider's job identifier, check its status and retrieve the result when complete. Uploading twice after a lost response can create two jobs unless the service provides an idempotency contract.

The audio leaves the machine in this workflow. Local playback and cached transcripts do not make recognition local. Retention, consent and access control must be addressed before using real recordings. A synthetic sample is adequate for checking the transport.

headingPath: Recognizing scanned recipes on a laptop
match.preview: Recognizing scanned recipes on a laptop Install the OCR engine and the required language packs ahead of time. Run recognition against local image files with networking disabled, then inspect uncertain words in the generated text. Images and

selectedFragments.text:
Recognizing scanned recipes on a laptop

Install the OCR engine and the required language packs ahead of time. Run recognition against local image files with networking disabled, then inspect uncertain words in the generated text. Images and extracted text stay on the laptop; no remote inference service is part of this workflow.

For old recipe cards, deskewing and contrast correction often matter more than changing the language model. Keep the original scan next to the corrected transcript. The first installation may require a download, so prepare the machine before taking it offline. Batch processing writes to a separate output directory and never overwrites the scans.

match.preview: A practical vocabulary review policy Ask the learner to produce a word from a meaning and context before displaying the answer. Record an unaided response as success; recognition after revealing it is an error for this exercise. After succe

selectedFragments.text:
A practical vocabulary review policy

Ask the learner to produce a word from a meaning and context before displaying the answer. Record an unaided response as success; recognition after revealing it is an error for this exercise. After success increase the interval, and after failure shorten it while checking whether the prompt was ambiguous.

Keep a daily workload ceiling and review persistent failures for multiple senses or missing examples. A card can be suspended and rewritten instead of drilled indefinitely. The policy combines the retrieval task with scheduling, so neither a long streak nor rapid clicking is the sole measure of learning.

match.preview: Producing an answer from memory Recognition is an unreliable rehearsal for speaking. Close the book, look at a meaning or situation, and try to supply the foreign expression before revealing it. A failed attempt followed by corrective feedb

selectedFragments.text:
Producing an answer from memory

Recognition is an unreliable rehearsal for speaking. Close the book, look at a meaning or situation, and try to supply the foreign expression before revealing it. A failed attempt followed by corrective feedback exposes what still needs practice. Saying that a sentence looks familiar is a different task.

Keep cards small enough to identify the missing knowledge. Alternate spoken and written production when both matter. An example sentence helps choose the intended sense, but should not reveal the answer through its first letters. Review outcomes should record whether the expression was produced unaided, not how pleasant the exercise felt.

headingPath: Hosted OCR for a shared archive
match.preview: Hosted OCR for a shared archive The archive team uploads scanned pages to a cloud OCR service and receives searchable text with confidence scores. A central queue makes it convenient to process large batches from several computers. Language

selectedFragments.text:
Hosted OCR for a shared archive

The archive team uploads scanned pages to a cloud OCR service and receives searchable text with confidence scores. A central queue makes it convenient to process large batches from several computers. Language detection and layout analysis are performed by the remote provider.

Local preprocessing can crop borders before upload, but the page contents still leave the computer. The retention policy and permission to transmit the material must be decided beforehand. This is not an offline workflow. Failed jobs keep their provider identifiers so an operator can inspect their status instead of resubmitting a whole batch.

selectedFragments.text:
План языкового семестра > Домашняя работа

Чтение готовит контекст для обсуждения. Новые выражения записываются вместе с коротким примером, а трудные места разбираются на встрече. Можно перечитать знакомый рассказ для беглости, но проверку самостоятельного воспроизведения слов проводят отдельно. Если ученик пропустил неделю, преподаватель сокращает объём, сохраняя регулярность. Быстрое завершение всех карточек не заменяет содержательного ответа.

match.preview: Reading a chapter twice The first pass through a chapter establishes the topic. On the second pass, underline unfamiliar words and inspect how clauses fit together. This can improve comprehension and make later reading feel more fluent. It

selectedFragments.text:
Reading a chapter twice

The first pass through a chapter establishes the topic. On the second pass, underline unfamiliar words and inspect how clauses fit together. This can improve comprehension and make later reading feel more fluent. It is useful when the goal is following the author's argument.

Familiarity with a paragraph does not demonstrate that its vocabulary can be produced in conversation. Highlighting everything removes its usefulness as a signal. A reading log records the chapter, the questions that remain and one sentence worth discussing with a tutor.

match.preview: Searching by meaning Dense embeddings place passages with related meanings near each other even when their wording differs. Search embeds the question and ranks stored vectors by similarity. A document with several passages can be represent

selectedFragments.text:
Searching by meaning

Dense embeddings place passages with related meanings near each other even when their wording differs. Search embeds the question and ranks stored vectors by similarity. A document with several passages can be represented by several vectors, with the best match determining its document score.

This is useful for remembered ideas and cross-language discovery. Rare codes and exact numbers may not be preserved strongly enough for identifier lookup. A subsequent reranker can reorder retrieved passages, but cannot recover a document absent from its candidate pool.

match.preview: Shadowing a short recording Listen to a short passage and speak along just behind the recording. This encourages attention to rhythm, linking and stress. Start with a passage whose meaning is already understood so that decoding the story do

selectedFragments.text:
Shadowing a short recording

Listen to a short passage and speak along just behind the recording. This encourages attention to rhythm, linking and stress. Start with a passage whose meaning is already understood so that decoding the story does not consume all attention.

Record a brief attempt and compare one feature at a time. Fluent imitation does not necessarily demonstrate perception of a particular vowel contrast. Alternate shadowing with other activities rather than using speed as the only success measure. Rest the voice when the exercise becomes strained.

match.preview: Configuration without pasted secrets A local development process can read a credential from a restricted file or receive it through its environment. The value should stay out of command arguments, source files and logs. Diagnostics can repo

selectedFragments.text:
Configuration without pasted secrets

A local development process can read a credential from a restricted file or receive it through its environment. The value should stay out of command arguments, source files and logs. Diagnostics can report whether loading succeeded without printing the credential.

An environment variable is not magical encryption: child processes may inherit it and local inspection may reveal it. Limit the process lifetime and remove unnecessary inheritance. Synthetic test data reduces exposure if a remote integration must be exercised.

match.preview: The response vanished after submission Before sending an external job, persist its stable operation identifier and a reserved state. If the connection closes after transmission, mark the outcome unknown. Ask the provider for the receipt usi

selectedFragments.text:
The response vanished after submission

Before sending an external job, persist its stable operation identifier and a reserved state. If the connection closes after transmission, mark the outcome unknown. Ask the provider for the receipt using that identifier before considering another submission. A missing client response is not proof that the provider did no work or charged nothing.

Keep confirmed, failed-before-send and uncertain states distinct. A local process restart reloads the ledger and blocks uncertain operations. Where the provider has no lookup or idempotency guarantee, manual reconciliation may be necessary. A new identifier would hide the uncertainty rather than resolve it.

headingPath: A name that remains missing after publication
match.preview: A name that remains missing after publication Resolvers cache negative answers as well as successful lookups. After an NXDOMAIN response, a newly created DNS record may remain invisible to that resolver until the negative cache lifetime exp

selectedFragments.text:
A name that remains missing after publication

Resolvers cache negative answers as well as successful lookups. After an NXDOMAIN response, a newly created DNS record may remain invisible to that resolver until the negative cache lifetime expires. Inspect the authority information and the relevant cache rather than repeatedly editing the correct new record.

Test the authoritative server separately from the recursive resolver. A low TTL set after the negative answer does not retroactively erase caches that already hold it. Browser and operating-system caches can add another layer. Document the observation time so later tests can be compared meaningfully.

match.preview: Finding an exact diagnostic token For a literal identifier such as E_CONN_42, use an exact or lexical search that preserves underscores and digits. Inspect the tokenizer: some full-text indexes split punctuation, so a quoted phrase may stil

selectedFragments.text:
Finding an exact diagnostic token

For a literal identifier such as E_CONN_42, use an exact or lexical search that preserves underscores and digits. Inspect the tokenizer: some full-text indexes split punctuation, so a quoted phrase may still need a raw substring check. Exact identifiers are often rare and semantically opaque.

Vector similarity is useful for explanations expressed in different words, but can return a related error instead of the precise token. Offer lexical matching for this task and inspect the actual occurrence. Renaming the file to the token is unnecessary when its body is indexed correctly.

headingPath: Capturing a source while it exists
match.preview: Capturing a source while it exists A useful research note keeps the page address, author when known, capture date and a short exact excerpt beside the claim it supports. Save an allowed local snapshot if the source is likely to change. A ba

selectedFragments.text:
Capturing a source while it exists

A useful research note keeps the page address, author when known, capture date and a short exact excerpt beside the claim it supports. Save an allowed local snapshot if the source is likely to change. A bare bookmark can later lead to different wording or a missing page.

The note should say what was observed at capture time. Separate the source's words from an interpretation written later. When revisiting a changed page, retain the original citation and add the newer observation rather than silently replacing the evidence. Tags can help navigation, but do not preserve what a source actually said.

match.preview: Counting completed lessons A course dashboard records attendance, submitted exercises and time spent in the application. These measures help notice a broken routine or an assignment nobody opened. They are straightforward to collect without

selectedFragments.text:
Counting completed lessons

A course dashboard records attendance, submitted exercises and time spent in the application. These measures help notice a broken routine or an assignment nobody opened. They are straightforward to collect without judging every answer.

Completion does not measure whether a learner can distinguish similar vowels on an unfamiliar recording. A listening assessment needs its own task and scoring rule. Avoid turning minutes spent into a general proficiency score. Use the dashboard to start a conversation about study habits, not to replace direct evidence.

match.preview: A modest tagging vocabulary Tags work best when they express a few stable dimensions such as project, status and broad subject. A tag per sentence creates a second filing system that is harder to maintain than the notes themselves. Merge sy

selectedFragments.text:
A modest tagging vocabulary

Tags work best when they express a few stable dimensions such as project, status and broad subject. A tag per sentence creates a second filing system that is harder to maintain than the notes themselves. Merge synonyms during a periodic review rather than while capturing every thought.

Links carry specific relationships; tags collect loose families. Neither is a substitute for a source citation. An inbox can remain untagged until its contents are understood. Search should still work when the author has forgotten the exact tag.

headingPath: Слышать различие, а не угадывать слово
match.preview: Слышать различие, а не угадывать слово Для пары английских гласных полезно упражнение с минимальными парами: слушатель слышит один вариант и выбирает, какой из двух был произнесён. Например, ship и sheep различаются целевым звуком, а не общ

selectedFragments.text:
Слышать различие, а не угадывать слово

Для пары английских гласных полезно упражнение с минимальными парами: слушатель слышит один вариант и выбирает, какой из двух был произнесён. Например, ship и sheep различаются целевым звуком, а не общей темой фразы. Сначала используйте несколько дикторов, затем проверяйте перенос на незнакомые записи.

Показывайте ответ после выбора, иначе написание подсказывает решение. Считайте ошибки распознавания отдельно от качества собственного произношения. Медленное повторение за диктором тренирует артикуляцию, но само по себе не измеряет, научилось ли ухо различать звуки.

match.preview: Off-site version history An object store can retain previous versions after a file is overwritten or deleted. This protects against losing the local machine, provided credentials, retention and restore procedures are sound. Upload bandwidth

selectedFragments.text:
Off-site version history

An object store can retain previous versions after a file is overwritten or deleted. This protects against losing the local machine, provided credentials, retention and restore procedures are sound. Upload bandwidth and storage charges belong in the plan.

The workflow intentionally transfers files to a remote system. It does not meet a requirement that every backup stay on local disks. Encryption before upload changes confidentiality, not location. Test how a deleted object version is recovered before relying on the service.

selectedFragments.text:
Home archive operations > Recovery practice

Keep a written mount layout with backup locations, but do not place recovery secrets in the catalogue. Test recovery into a different directory. The local index is disposable and can be rebuilt once the archive identity is verified. A failed migration should leave both the original files and the previous catalogue available for inspection.

selectedFragments.text:
Importing a community catalogue > Character decoding

Decode bytes using an explicitly confirmed character encoding. A wrong encoding can turn names into replacement characters before the parser sees a single field. Inspect representative non-ASCII names and reject undecodable bytes rather than silently dropping them. Line endings may differ between systems. A byte-order mark should be handled by the decoder or parser according to its documented behavior, not removed from arbitrary positions.

headingPath: Keeping a backup out of the failure domain
match.preview: Keeping a backup out of the failure domain A disk permanently attached to the same writable system can be damaged by the same mistake or malicious process as the source. Rotate an offline local copy and retain several dated generations. Dis

selectedFragments.text:
Keeping a backup out of the failure domain

A disk permanently attached to the same writable system can be damaged by the same mistake or malicious process as the source. Rotate an offline local copy and retain several dated generations. Disconnect it after verification so ordinary deletions cannot immediately propagate to every copy.

This improves isolation but is not proof that the files can be restored or decrypted. A separate recovery rehearsal checks that. Decide how much recent work may be lost between rotations, label the generations, and inspect disk health without treating health statistics as a substitute for reading the data.

match.preview: Retryable and permanent failures A read request may be repeated after a temporary connection failure within a fixed deadline. Authentication failures and invalid input generally require a change before another attempt. A response telling th

selectedFragments.text:
Retryable and permanent failures

A read request may be repeated after a temporary connection failure within a fixed deadline. Authentication failures and invalid input generally require a change before another attempt. A response telling the client to slow down should influence scheduling.

Classifying a transport failure as temporary does not establish whether a remote write happened. The operation's repeat-safety contract must be checked separately. Collect attempt count and final status without logging credentials or full user payloads. Retry policy should remain bounded even during a long outage.

match.preview: Expanding review intervals Repeated retrieval should be separated in time. After an unaided correct response, lengthen the next interval; after an error, bring the item back sooner and inspect the prompt. Schedule by observed recall rather

selectedFragments.text:
Expanding review intervals

Repeated retrieval should be separated in time. After an unaided correct response, lengthen the next interval; after an error, bring the item back sooner and inspect the prompt. Schedule by observed recall rather than the date on which a card was created.

One fixed calendar for every word ignores differences in difficulty. A missed review is not a reason to restart the entire deck. Limit the daily workload and suspend ambiguous cards until they are rewritten. The scheduler determines when practice occurs; it cannot turn a recognition-only exercise into productive recall.

match.preview: A restore rehearsal Choose a dated backup generation and recover several files into an empty scratch directory. Compare their bytes or checksums with the expected versions, then open the formats people actually use. Test an accidentally del

selectedFragments.text:
A restore rehearsal

Choose a dated backup generation and recover several files into an empty scratch directory. Compare their bytes or checksums with the expected versions, then open the formats people actually use. Test an accidentally deleted file as well as a current one.

Record elapsed time, missing tools and every manual step needed to locate the right generation. A scheduled backup job reporting success is only evidence that the job ran. Recovery instructions should be understandable on a replacement machine. Never rehearse by overwriting the working originals.

headingPath: Can an encrypted backup be recovered?
match.preview: Can an encrypted backup be recovered? Encryption protects backup contents only if the recovery secret remains available to the owner. Store a recovery copy of that secret separately from the machine and verify that the documented unlock pro

selectedFragments.text:
Can an encrypted backup be recovered?

Encryption protects backup contents only if the recovery secret remains available to the owner. Store a recovery copy of that secret separately from the machine and verify that the documented unlock procedure works on a clean test environment. A successful upload or copy does not prove decryptability.

Restore a small representative sample to a separate location, open it and compare checksums. Include filenames with non-ASCII characters and a recently changed file. Record the backup generation used. The test should exercise the real recovery path, not merely confirm that an archive file exists.

match.preview: A consistent paginated export A cursor prevents positional drift but does not freeze records that are updated or removed during a long export. Pin a database snapshot or an immutable dataset version and bind every continuation token to that

selectedFragments.text:
A consistent paginated export

A cursor prevents positional drift but does not freeze records that are updated or removed during a long export. Pin a database snapshot or an immutable dataset version and bind every continuation token to that version, the filters and a unique sort order. Reject a token whose snapshot has expired rather than silently switching views.

For append-only data, a captured upper watermark may suffice if its assumptions are explicit. A timestamp alone is not enough when equal timestamps or backdated inserts are possible. Store export metadata next to the generated files so completeness can later be checked.

headingPath: Local snapshots that survive a mistaken deletion
match.preview: Local snapshots that survive a mistaken deletion Keep dated backup generations on a separate local disk. A snapshot tool can hard-link unchanged files while preserving older directory trees; deleting a source file must not remove its prior

selectedFragments.text:
Local snapshots that survive a mistaken deletion

Keep dated backup generations on a separate local disk. A snapshot tool can hard-link unchanged files while preserving older directory trees; deleting a source file must not remove its prior generations. Retention removes old snapshots only according to an explicit schedule.

A synchronized mirror usually propagates deletions, so it cannot by itself recover yesterday's accidentally removed file. Verify a restore into another folder and disconnect the backup disk after the job. Hard links save space only for unchanged content; editing files in a snapshot in place can damage shared data. Treat completed generations as immutable.

headingPath: Keeping a backup out of the failure domain
match.preview: Keeping a backup out of the failure domain A disk permanently attached to the same writable system can be damaged by the same mistake or malicious process as the source. Rotate an offline local copy and retain several dated generations. Dis

selectedFragments.text:
Keeping a backup out of the failure domain

A disk permanently attached to the same writable system can be damaged by the same mistake or malicious process as the source. Rotate an offline local copy and retain several dated generations. Disconnect it after verification so ordinary deletions cannot immediately propagate to every copy.

This improves isolation but is not proof that the files can be restored or decrypted. A separate recovery rehearsal checks that. Decide how much recent work may be lost between rotations, label the generations, and inspect disk health without treating health statistics as a substitute for reading the data.

match.preview: A restore rehearsal Choose a dated backup generation and recover several files into an empty scratch directory. Compare their bytes or checksums with the expected versions, then open the formats people actually use. Test an accidentally del

selectedFragments.text:
A restore rehearsal

Choose a dated backup generation and recover several files into an empty scratch directory. Compare their bytes or checksums with the expected versions, then open the formats people actually use. Test an accidentally deleted file as well as a current one.

Record elapsed time, missing tools and every manual step needed to locate the right generation. A scheduled backup job reporting success is only evidence that the job ran. Recovery instructions should be understandable on a replacement machine. Never rehearse by overwriting the working originals.

match.preview: Off-site version history An object store can retain previous versions after a file is overwritten or deleted. This protects against losing the local machine, provided credentials, retention and restore procedures are sound. Upload bandwidth

selectedFragments.text:
Off-site version history

An object store can retain previous versions after a file is overwritten or deleted. This protects against losing the local machine, provided credentials, retention and restore procedures are sound. Upload bandwidth and storage charges belong in the plan.

The workflow intentionally transfers files to a remote system. It does not meet a requirement that every backup stay on local disks. Encryption before upload changes confidentiality, not location. Test how a deleted object version is recovered before relying on the service.

match.preview: Home archive operations > Recovery practice Keep a written mount layout with backup locations, but do not place recovery secrets in the catalogue. Test recovery into a different directory. The local index is disposable and can be rebuilt on

selectedFragments.text:
Home archive operations > Recovery practice

Keep a written mount layout with backup locations, but do not place recovery secrets in the catalogue. Test recovery into a different directory. The local index is disposable and can be rebuilt once the archive identity is verified. A failed migration should leave both the original files and the previous catalogue available for inspection.

headingPath: Can an encrypted backup be recovered?
match.preview: Can an encrypted backup be recovered? Encryption protects backup contents only if the recovery secret remains available to the owner. Store a recovery copy of that secret separately from the machine and verify that the documented unlock pro

selectedFragments.text:
Can an encrypted backup be recovered?

Encryption protects backup contents only if the recovery secret remains available to the owner. Store a recovery copy of that secret separately from the machine and verify that the documented unlock procedure works on a clean test environment. A successful upload or copy does not prove decryptability.

Restore a small representative sample to a separate location, open it and compare checksums. Include filenames with non-ASCII characters and a recently changed file. Record the backup generation used. The test should exercise the real recovery path, not merely confirm that an archive file exists.

match.preview: Mounting an extra disk Create a mount point and mount the intended filesystem there before copying files. Device names may change after reboot, so persistent filesystem identifiers are useful in configuration. Check available capacity and p

selectedFragments.text:
Mounting an extra disk

Create a mount point and mount the intended filesystem there before copying files. Device names may change after reboot, so persistent filesystem identifiers are useful in configuration. Check available capacity and permissions with a small disposable file.

Formatting a device destroys its old filesystem and belongs to initial setup, not routine recovery. This checklist does not define how an existing catalogue should react when its expected disk is missing. A directory's existence alone says little about which volume is attached to it.

headingPath: A mirror for two working folders
match.preview: A mirror for two working folders Bidirectional synchronization aims to make two active folders agree. Deletions and renames propagate according to its conflict rules. This is convenient for continuing work on another machine but can spread

selectedFragments.text:
A mirror for two working folders

Bidirectional synchronization aims to make two active folders agree. Deletions and renames propagate according to its conflict rules. This is convenient for continuing work on another machine but can spread an accidental removal to both sides.

Some products retain versions, yet that must be checked separately from the fact that synchronization succeeds. A green status means the mirror is current, not that historical files are recoverable. Keep conflicts visible and choose a separate backup policy when old states matter.

headingPath: Reconstructing state from an event log
match.preview: Reconstructing state from an event log An append-only sequence of accepted events can rebuild a projection after a crash. Save a projection checkpoint only after its state is durable, then replay events after that position. Event identity a

selectedFragments.text:
Reconstructing state from an event log

An append-only sequence of accepted events can rebuild a projection after a crash. Save a projection checkpoint only after its state is durable, then replay events after that position. Event identity and ordering rules matter when delivery is repeated.

Replaying a projection is different from resubmitting an external action. The event records what was accepted, while a vanished remote response may leave that fact unknown. Keep side effects out of an unguarded replay loop. Snapshots speed recovery but should be verifiable against their log position.

match.preview: Hard links and symbolic links A hard link names the same underlying file data within a filesystem. A symbolic link stores a path that is resolved when followed. Moving a target can break a symbolic link, while editing data through one hard

selectedFragments.text:
Hard links and symbolic links

A hard link names the same underlying file data within a filesystem. A symbolic link stores a path that is resolved when followed. Moving a target can break a symbolic link, while editing data through one hard link affects the shared file.

Neither link creates an independent backup copy. Snapshot tools using hard links must treat completed generations as immutable. A symbolic link to a mount point does not prove the desired disk is present there. Choose links for navigation or storage layout only after understanding these identity rules.

match.preview: Transcribing a practice recording locally A speech recognizer can process an audio file on the workstation when its model files are already available. Run a short synthetic recording first and inspect the transcript manually. The transcript

selectedFragments.text:
Transcribing a practice recording locally

A speech recognizer can process an audio file on the workstation when its model files are already available. Run a short synthetic recording first and inspect the transcript manually. The transcription process can then run with the network disconnected.

This workflow accepts audio, not scanned pages. It needs enough memory and compute for the selected model. Keep the original recording and avoid treating a plausible transcript as a verbatim record without review. Downloading model files is preparation, separate from sending recordings to a service.

match.preview: Reclaiming space in SQLite Deleting rows usually leaves pages available for reuse inside the database file. VACUUM rebuilds the database to compact it, requiring temporary disk space and coordination with other activity. It is a maintenance

selectedFragments.text:
Reclaiming space in SQLite

Deleting rows usually leaves pages available for reuse inside the database file. VACUUM rebuilds the database to compact it, requiring temporary disk space and coordination with other activity. It is a maintenance operation, not a way to make continuous readers coexist with writes.

Schedule compaction after checking file growth and operational needs. Automatic vacuum settings have different overhead and must be chosen deliberately. Keeping a small file on disk is not always worth a disruptive rebuild. Backups and integrity checks serve separate purposes.

headingPath: Hosted OCR for a shared archive
match.preview: Hosted OCR for a shared archive The archive team uploads scanned pages to a cloud OCR service and receives searchable text with confidence scores. A central queue makes it convenient to process large batches from several computers. Language

selectedFragments.text:
Hosted OCR for a shared archive

The archive team uploads scanned pages to a cloud OCR service and receives searchable text with confidence scores. A central queue makes it convenient to process large batches from several computers. Language detection and layout analysis are performed by the remote provider.

Local preprocessing can crop borders before upload, but the page contents still leave the computer. The retention policy and permission to transmit the material must be decided beforehand. This is not an offline workflow. Failed jobs keep their provider identifiers so an operator can inspect their status instead of resubmitting a whole batch.

match.preview: Configuration without pasted secrets A local development process can read a credential from a restricted file or receive it through its environment. The value should stay out of command arguments, source files and logs. Diagnostics can repo

selectedFragments.text:
Configuration without pasted secrets

A local development process can read a credential from a restricted file or receive it through its environment. The value should stay out of command arguments, source files and logs. Diagnostics can report whether loading succeeded without printing the credential.

An environment variable is not magical encryption: child processes may inherit it and local inspection may reveal it. Limit the process lifetime and remove unnecessary inheritance. Synthetic test data reduces exposure if a remote integration must be exercised.

match.preview: Compressing a collection for transfer An archive preserves a collection of paths while compression reduces repeated byte patterns. Already compressed photographs often shrink little. Choose a format that the receiving machine can open and v

selectedFragments.text:
Compressing a collection for transfer

An archive preserves a collection of paths while compression reduces repeated byte patterns. Already compressed photographs often shrink little. Choose a format that the receiving machine can open and verify the archive checksum after transfer.

Compression is not encryption or version history. Removing originals immediately after creating an archive eliminates an independent copy. Test extraction into an empty directory and check how the tool handles unusual filenames. A smaller file is useful only if its contents remain recoverable.

match.preview: Storing identical content once Content-addressed storage hashes file bytes and keeps one blob for identical content. Several logical documents can refer to that blob. Reference counts or a reachability scan determine when an unreferenced bl

selectedFragments.text:
Storing identical content once

Content-addressed storage hashes file bytes and keeps one blob for identical content. Several logical documents can refer to that blob. Reference counts or a reachability scan determine when an unreferenced blob may be removed.

This deduplicates storage, not business operations. Two commands with identical bodies may represent two intended actions, while a retried command may have a different timestamp. Hash collisions and normalization rules require explicit treatment. A file manifest preserves names and metadata independently of the blob identity.

match.preview: note-013 A travel laptop can recognize photographed labels after the OCR binary and language files have been installed. The local command takes an image path and writes text to a sibling file. Disconnecting the network during a trial confir

selectedFragments.text:
A travel laptop can recognize photographed labels after the OCR binary and language files have been installed. The local command takes an image path and writes text to a sibling file. Disconnecting the network during a trial confirms that recognition itself has no server dependency.

This note is a compact field checklist, not an installation guide. Check that the expected language pack exists, retain the photo, and correct uncertain characters manually. Downloading missing components while travelling may be impossible. A translation service is a separate step and may send the resulting text elsewhere.

selectedFragments.text:
Importing a community catalogue > Commit and recovery

Write the accepted batch into a transaction or a new generation and publish it only after validation finishes. A crash should leave the previous catalogue usable. The import log records source checksum, parser settings and rejected row identifiers. A corrected batch receives its own identity rather than overwriting the evidence of the failed attempt.

headingPath: Durable progress in a batch converter
match.preview: Durable progress in a batch converter Our image converter processes a directory overnight. It writes each completed output to a temporary file, verifies it, then renames it and records the input checksum and completed position in a durable

selectedFragments.text:
Durable progress in a batch converter

Our image converter processes a directory overnight. It writes each completed output to a temporary file, verifies it, then renames it and records the input checksum and completed position in a durable checkpoint. On restart it verifies recorded outputs and continues from the last committed boundary rather than beginning the directory again.

The checkpoint and output must agree. A counter advanced before a file is durable could skip work after a power loss. This design handles local, repeatable transformations. An external paid action whose response disappeared needs a receipt lookup; a local checkpoint alone cannot establish whether that action happened.

headingPath: Rejecting stale edits without a held lock
match.preview: Rejecting stale edits without a held lock Read a record together with its revision. Submit the update with that expected revision, and make the database replace it only if the revision still matches. Increment the revision on success; zero

selectedFragments.text:
Rejecting stale edits without a held lock

Read a record together with its revision. Submit the update with that expected revision, and make the database replace it only if the revision still matches. Increment the revision on success; zero affected rows means someone else changed the record and the editor must reload or merge.

This compare-and-swap pattern prevents a lost update without keeping a lock throughout a person's editing session. A timestamp with poor precision is a weak substitute for a revision counter. The conflict belongs in the user workflow; blindly retrying the old replacement would erase the protection.

headingPath: Recognizing scanned recipes on a laptop
match.preview: Recognizing scanned recipes on a laptop Install the OCR engine and the required language packs ahead of time. Run recognition against local image files with networking disabled, then inspect uncertain words in the generated text. Images and

selectedFragments.text:
Recognizing scanned recipes on a laptop

Install the OCR engine and the required language packs ahead of time. Run recognition against local image files with networking disabled, then inspect uncertain words in the generated text. Images and extracted text stay on the laptop; no remote inference service is part of this workflow.

For old recipe cards, deskewing and contrast correction often matter more than changing the language model. Keep the original scan next to the corrected transcript. The first installation may require a download, so prepare the machine before taking it offline. Batch processing writes to a separate output directory and never overwrites the scans.

match.preview: Recovery traffic after an outage When many clients wake together, doubling every waiting interval still leaves them in step. Our load rehearsal had quiet gaps followed by sharp bursts. Give each caller an independently sampled pause between

selectedFragments.text:
Recovery traffic after an outage

When many clients wake together, doubling every waiting interval still leaves them in step. Our load rehearsal had quiet gaps followed by sharp bursts. Give each caller an independently sampled pause between zero and its current ceiling. Increase that ceiling after a failure, with a cap and an overall deadline. Spread the arrivals instead of merely postponing the crowd.

The random generator should not receive the same seed in every container. Record attempt counts and elapsed time, not just the final status. A server hint may impose a minimum wait. This is traffic shaping during recovery; it does not make a side effect safe to execute twice.

headingPath: A dictionary for a disconnected trip
match.preview: A dictionary for a disconnected trip Download a licensed dictionary database before departure and open it with a local reader. Word lookup then uses only the stored database and needs neither an account nor a network connection. The sentenc

selectedFragments.text:
A dictionary for a disconnected trip

Download a licensed dictionary database before departure and open it with a local reader. Word lookup then uses only the stored database and needs neither an account nor a network connection. The sentence being read is not submitted to a translation website.

Test inflected forms and the languages you need while still at home. A bilingual dictionary offers meanings and examples, but will not rewrite an entire paragraph idiomatically. Keep a small list of unresolved usages for later study. Disable optional online suggestions if the reader offers them.

match.preview: Remote transcription queue A hosted speech service accepts uploaded recordings and returns transcripts asynchronously. Store the provider's job identifier, check its status and retrieve the result when complete. Uploading twice after a lost

selectedFragments.text:
Remote transcription queue

A hosted speech service accepts uploaded recordings and returns transcripts asynchronously. Store the provider's job identifier, check its status and retrieve the result when complete. Uploading twice after a lost response can create two jobs unless the service provides an idempotency contract.

The audio leaves the machine in this workflow. Local playback and cached transcripts do not make recognition local. Retention, consent and access control must be addressed before using real recordings. A synthetic sample is adequate for checking the transport.

selectedFragments.text:
Срок жизни ответов DNS

Рекурсивный сервер сохраняет ответы на ограниченное время. Отрицательный ответ о несуществующем имени тоже может попасть в кеш. Поэтому запись, созданная после неудачного запроса, иногда становится видна не сразу.

Сравните ответ авторитетного сервера с ответом используемого резолвера. Повторное сохранение уже правильной записи не очищает чужой кеш. Успешный ответ из другой сети помогает локализовать проблему, но сам по себе не доказывает, какой именно кеш задерживает обновление.

match.preview: SQLite readers during normal writes Write-ahead logging lets a read transaction see a stable snapshot while another connection appends changes. Enable WAL mode deliberately, keep read transactions short, and let checkpointing reclaim the lo

selectedFragments.text:
SQLite readers during normal writes

Write-ahead logging lets a read transaction see a stable snapshot while another connection appends changes. Enable WAL mode deliberately, keep read transactions short, and let checkpointing reclaim the log when readers release their snapshots. This provides live queries without copying database files or holding a long exclusive lock against writers.

There is still only one writer at a time. Long readers can prevent checkpoint progress and make the WAL file grow. Treat the database, WAL and shared-memory files as a coordinated system; copying one live file is not a backup procedure. Measure transaction duration before tuning timeouts.

match.preview: Restarting a disposable build The documentation preview is built in a temporary directory. If compilation fails, discard that directory and run the build from its clean inputs. No user edits live there, and outputs are cheap to regenerate.

selectedFragments.text:
Restarting a disposable build

The documentation preview is built in a temporary directory. If compilation fails, discard that directory and run the build from its clean inputs. No user edits live there, and outputs are cheap to regenerate. This avoids complicated partial-state recovery.

The strategy is unsuitable for an overnight conversion whose completed files are expensive to recreate. Keep the build input revision and compiler version in the log. A successful build replaces the published preview atomically, so visitors never see a half-written page.

headingPath: A name that remains missing after publication
match.preview: A name that remains missing after publication Resolvers cache negative answers as well as successful lookups. After an NXDOMAIN response, a newly created DNS record may remain invisible to that resolver until the negative cache lifetime exp

selectedFragments.text:
A name that remains missing after publication

Resolvers cache negative answers as well as successful lookups. After an NXDOMAIN response, a newly created DNS record may remain invisible to that resolver until the negative cache lifetime expires. Inspect the authority information and the relevant cache rather than repeatedly editing the correct new record.

Test the authoritative server separately from the recursive resolver. A low TTL set after the negative answer does not retroactively erase caches that already hold it. Browser and operating-system caches can add another layer. Document the observation time so later tests can be compared meaningfully.

match.preview: A consistent paginated export A cursor prevents positional drift but does not freeze records that are updated or removed during a long export. Pin a database snapshot or an immutable dataset version and bind every continuation token to that

selectedFragments.text:
A consistent paginated export

A cursor prevents positional drift but does not freeze records that are updated or removed during a long export. Pin a database snapshot or an immutable dataset version and bind every continuation token to that version, the filters and a unique sort order. Reject a token whose snapshot has expired rather than silently switching views.

For append-only data, a captured upper watermark may suffice if its assumptions are explicit. A timestamp alone is not enough when equal timestamps or backdated inserts are possible. Store export metadata next to the generated files so completeness can later be checked.

match.preview: Finding an exact diagnostic token For a literal identifier such as E_CONN_42, use an exact or lexical search that preserves underscores and digits. Inspect the tokenizer: some full-text indexes split punctuation, so a quoted phrase may stil

selectedFragments.text:
Finding an exact diagnostic token

For a literal identifier such as E_CONN_42, use an exact or lexical search that preserves underscores and digits. Inspect the tokenizer: some full-text indexes split punctuation, so a quoted phrase may still need a raw substring check. Exact identifiers are often rare and semantically opaque.

Vector similarity is useful for explanations expressed in different words, but can return a related error instead of the precise token. Offer lexical matching for this task and inspect the actual occurrence. Renaming the file to the token is unnecessary when its body is indexed correctly.

selectedFragments.text:
One purchase, one operation identity

Assign an idempotency key to a business operation before its first POST. Store the key with a hash of the parameters and the eventual result on the server. A retry with the same key and same parameters returns that recorded result instead of creating a second purchase. Reusing the key for different parameters is rejected.

Deduplicating identical files or comparing request bodies is insufficient: two intentional purchases can have identical details. The identity must survive a client restart. If the first response is lost, query that identity or retry only under the server's documented idempotency contract.

match.preview: The response vanished after submission Before sending an external job, persist its stable operation identifier and a reserved state. If the connection closes after transmission, mark the outcome unknown. Ask the provider for the receipt usi

selectedFragments.text:
The response vanished after submission

Before sending an external job, persist its stable operation identifier and a reserved state. If the connection closes after transmission, mark the outcome unknown. Ask the provider for the receipt using that identifier before considering another submission. A missing client response is not proof that the provider did no work or charged nothing.

Keep confirmed, failed-before-send and uncertain states distinct. A local process restart reloads the ledger and blocks uncertain operations. Where the provider has no lookup or idempotency guarantee, manual reconciliation may be necessary. A new identifier would hide the uncertainty rather than resolve it.

match.preview: Storing identical content once Content-addressed storage hashes file bytes and keeps one blob for identical content. Several logical documents can refer to that blob. Reference counts or a reachability scan determine when an unreferenced bl

selectedFragments.text:
Storing identical content once

Content-addressed storage hashes file bytes and keeps one blob for identical content. Several logical documents can refer to that blob. Reference counts or a reachability scan determine when an unreferenced blob may be removed.

This deduplicates storage, not business operations. Two commands with identical bodies may represent two intended actions, while a retried command may have a different timestamp. Hash collisions and normalization rules require explicit treatment. A file manifest preserves names and metadata independently of the blob identity.

match.preview: Service handover notebook > Publication barrier Every new claim receives a monotonically increasing fencing number. The storage layer remembers the largest number accepted for the resource and rejects writes carrying an older number. Lease

selectedFragments.text:
Service handover notebook > Publication barrier

Every new claim receives a monotonically increasing fencing number. The storage layer remembers the largest number accepted for the resource and rejects writes carrying an older number. Lease expiry alone cannot stop a paused former owner from publishing after a successor has taken over; the resource must enforce this fence when committing the effect. Check the number and write the result atomically. A heartbeat timestamp checked only by the worker is insufficient.

The sequence must survive scheduler restarts. Reusing an old number would allow a delayed write to look current. Keep failed fence checks visible as stale-worker events rather than retrying them as transient storage errors. This rule is about authority of a writer, not deduplication of identical image bytes.

headingPath: Rejecting stale edits without a held lock
match.preview: Rejecting stale edits without a held lock Read a record together with its revision. Submit the update with that expected revision, and make the database replace it only if the revision still matches. Increment the revision on success; zero

selectedFragments.text:
Rejecting stale edits without a held lock

Read a record together with its revision. Submit the update with that expected revision, and make the database replace it only if the revision still matches. Increment the revision on success; zero affected rows means someone else changed the record and the editor must reload or merge.

This compare-and-swap pattern prevents a lost update without keeping a lock throughout a person's editing session. A timestamp with poor precision is a weak substitute for a revision counter. The conflict belongs in the user workflow; blindly retrying the old replacement would erase the protection.

selectedFragments.text:
Retryable and permanent failures

A read request may be repeated after a temporary connection failure within a fixed deadline. Authentication failures and invalid input generally require a change before another attempt. A response telling the client to slow down should influence scheduling.

Classifying a transport failure as temporary does not establish whether a remote write happened. The operation's repeat-safety contract must be checked separately. Collect attempt count and final status without logging credentials or full user payloads. Retry policy should remain bounded even during a long outage.

selectedFragments.text:
Importing a community catalogue > Commit and recovery

Write the accepted batch into a transaction or a new generation and publish it only after validation finishes. A crash should leave the previous catalogue usable. The import log records source checksum, parser settings and rejected row identifiers. A corrected batch receives its own identity rather than overwriting the evidence of the failed attempt.
